title: Fighting Depression With Thai Snacks and Art
summary: This official vlog moves through depression, anhedonia and medication/appetite tradeoffs into cheap art-material hunting, Thai Town desserts and a fast no-sketch painting session. The 246-decision layer repairs oops paint, cull/cutoff lumber, Thai Town, matcha, grass jelly, taro, sticky rice, banana leaf, Thai tea, pandan and likely ruam mit while leaving the shop/product name and damaged prices unresolved. It preserves rapid weight loss and on-medication self-report without endorsing a skinny/healthy equation or medical choice. A separate thrift vlog says Choe recently stopped all medication; recording chronology is unknown, so both statements remain dated and unsynthesized. Retail security codes and nunchuck-like assembly stay raw-only. Direct craft evidence includes found-color constraints, no-plan shapes, a stopping heuristic, drying/airbrush, dog subject and self-compassion.

connections.relationship: Lower production is framed as a more direct everyday record.
Aimless movement through big-box stores becomes a personal routine during depression.
Lack of appetite and pleasure is separated from the food’s quality.
Choe links appetite change to medication without clinical verification.
The speaker experiences treatment as skinny/depressed versus fat/not depressed, a frame the archive must not endorse.
A major audience milestone fails to produce excitement, sharpening the anhedonia evidence.
Choe declines to judge the restaurant while his taste and desire feel blunted.
The vlog shifts from health reflection to constraint-based material search.
Rejected/mistinted paint becomes a palette-selection system rather than a compromise.
Cheap available material leads the creative decision instead of serving a preplanned color.
The spray-paint cabinet discussion must remain raw-only rather than searchable technique.
Scrap wood becomes an alternative drawing/painting support.
The source corrects the older free-scrap memory to a displayed 70%-off rule.
Public-restroom filming and bystander objection create a consent/privacy boundary.
The episode repeatedly revises the total from roughly $24 to $26 and should preserve uncertainty.
Food search becomes another attempt to recover sensory pleasure and memory.
This directly conflicts with the separate thrift vlog’s recent off-all-medication report.
A damaged Thai dessert name is likely ruam mit but needs native/menu confirmation.
Choe eats for the vlog despite saying he has no appetite, then reports strong sensory response.
Snack spending and sweetness become a medical-cost joke, not diagnosis.
Unwrapping and texture provide the clearest food-object documentation.
Feeling somewhat better becomes eagerness to begin the art project, not proof of treatment.
The prop’s weapon framing is immediately revised; assembly remains restricted.
Cheap colors prompt immediate shapes without sketching.
Asking whether the painting is finished becomes a cue to stop.
When uncertain, Choe returns to painting his dog.
Impatience and wet paint are followed by an explicit decision to be gentle with himself.
The response to ‘a child could do that’ is an invitation to try, not an art-status defense.
Choe separates external circumstances from the wet-blanket feeling.
Making, movement, kindness, food and sharing form a personal action bundle.
Childhood Lego destruction/giving becomes a model for making without monetizing every object.
The apparent placement of valuable paintings is revealed as only for show.
